title: Oral late effects of treatment for childhood and adolescent cancer
summary: More people than ever survive cancer diagnosed during childhood and adolescence. However, cancer treatment can have long-term effects on health, including teeth, jaws and oral health. This study aims to assess oral and dental health among adults who were treated for cancer during childhood or adolescence. Information from questionnaires will be combined with findings from dental examinations. The study seeks to improve knowledge about risks and to support better long-term follow-up care.
conditions: Late effects after childhood and adolescent cancer

interventions.name: Adult survivors of childhood and adolescent cancer registered in the German Childhood Cancer Registry (GCCR). All participants complete a questionnaire assessing oral health, oral health-related quality of life, dental care utilization and health-related quality of life. A randomly selected subgroup

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Diagnosis of a childhood cancer classified according to ICCC-3 between ages 0 and 17 years
• Registered in the German Childhood Cancer Registry (GCCR)
• At least 5-year survival after primary cancer diagnosis
• Age ≥ 18 years at study entry
• Residence in the Rhine-Main region, Germany
• Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
• Not included in the long-term follow-up program of the German Childhood Cancer Registry (GCCR)
• No written informed consent
